answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay, and within 15 minutes once the operator knows or should know that a death has occurred at the mine. The call goes to the toll-free number 1-800-746-1553.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay, and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once the operator knows or should know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the covered accidents.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must have an incombustible content of not less than 80 percent. The required percentage rises only where methane is present.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: The self-rescue device made available to each miner who goes underground must be adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months. They must be held for each shift, at some time other than a shift change, and involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: Under 30 CFR 48.5 (underground miners), each new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA. This is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. This applies under both 56.9300 and 57.9300.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (30 CFR 56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in 30 CFR 57.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plans. They cover only MSHA respirable dust control plans and respiratory protection programs for mines.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The chunks don't say. They cover mine slopes and shafts, bucket requirements for shaft sinking, and rollover protective structures. None of them covers OSHA construction trench protective systems or a depth threshold for shoring or trench boxes.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover other matters: impoundment design plans, permits for mining under bodies of water, and permits for experimental equipment.
